terms.x: what a for loop asks for
terms.p: The trait that says a value can be turned into an iterator, which is the only thing a for loop knows how to consume.
A range that includes its start and excludes its end, so its length is always the end minus the start and adjacent ranges never overlap.
An extra condition attached to a match arm, tested after the pattern matches, and ignored by the compiler's check that every case is covered.
An expression that does not produce a value because control leaves instead, by returning, breaking, continuing or panicking.
A break that names an enclosing loop or block, so it exits that one rather than the innermost one.
A let that binds a pattern when it matches and otherwise runs a block that must leave the function, so the binding is usable in everything that follows.
The simpler form a piece of convenient syntax expands into before the compiler type-checks it.
